generatedProse.concept-context: In sport and exercise science this shapes everything from a training-study report to an essay on coaching. Before writing, you remind yourself how the field reports data, defines its terms precisely, and ties claims to measured results. As you draft, you bring studies in to back your argument and show where you are judging their strength, not just repeating them. Each piece builds a clearer sense of what the field expects of you.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two sport science students write up the same training study. One writes loosely and claims the programme 'clearly works' without tying the claim to the data. The other has read widely in the field, matches its precise, data-tied style, and uses the study to support a measured claim of his own. His write-up reads like sport science, because he has recognised the conventions, learned them from his reading, and used them with a critical edge in one practice.
generatedProse.summary: In sport and exercise science, writing as a member of the field is a continuing practice. You recognise its conventions, learn them by reading studies as a writer, and integrate sources with a critical edge so your own argument leads. Repeated on every assignment, it is what makes your writing read as the work of someone inside the field.

check.body: A student notices that history essays argue in the writer's own voice, reads several to confirm it, then drafts a paragraph that opens in her own voice and uses a source to support her point. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first programme, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next programme.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next programme, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next programme improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That she is running the three strands as one practice: recognising a convention, confirming it by reading, then writing to it with a critical edge.
_items.feedback: Yes. She moved through all three strands, one after another, as one connected practice.

_items.text: That she has memorised a set of rules that apply to every subject.
_items.feedback: The conventions she used belong to history, not to every subject.

_items.text: That reading published work replaces the need to write anything of her own.
_items.feedback: She still wrote her own paragraph; reading informed it rather than replacing it.

_items.text: That recognising a convention is all that matters, and the drafting is optional.
_items.feedback: Recognising the convention was only the first strand; she then read and drafted too.
